text:
Marathon Petroleum shares have fallen 18.5% over two weeks, with today's decline fitting into a sharp drop that accelerated after the company's quarterly earnings report on November 3rd. The broader headwind is clear: the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections has sparked investor concerns about renewable energy policy favoring and fossil fuel regulation tightening, which directly threatens refining company valuations regardless of current oil or refining conditions (US crude is still trading at $99.64 per barrel and refineries are running at 94.5% capacity).

The timing and magnitude of the sell-off suggest investors are repricing the long-term outlook for petroleum refiners in a political environment now tilted toward wind and solar investment. Even though global oil prices remain elevated at $107 and storage levels are stable, refining stocks face structural headwinds from this shift in energy policy momentum.
